answers.evidence:
Repro of the original panic (build-tagged buggy variant):

```
$ go run -tags buggy . du
panic: unable to redefine 'h' shorthand in "du" flagset: it's already used for "human" flag
  ... github.com/spf13/pflag.(*FlagSet).AddFlag ... flag.go:902
  ... cobra.(*Command).InitDefaultHelpFlag ... command.go:1229   <- auto -h collides
```

Fixed CLI, all verified live:

```
$ go run . du --help        # -h/--help intact, --human long-only, -d free
Flags:
  -d, --depth int   descend at most N levels of directories
  -h, --help        help for du
      --human       print sizes in human readable format
Global Flags:
  -o, --output string   write output to FILE ('-' for stdout) (default "-")

$ go run . du -h | head -1 # help, no panic
estimate file space usage

$ go run . du -d 2 --human tmp
du called: human=true depth=2 output="-" args=[tmp]

$ go run . du -o out.txt   # parent persistent -o inherited, no collision
du called: human=false depth=0 output="out.txt" args=[]
```

Test suite (`go vet` clean, `gofmt` clean, `go test -race` passes):

```
=== RUN   TestHelpSmokePerSubcommand            PASS  (root+3 subcommands × --help/-h = 10 smoke invocations)
=== RUN   TestLongFlagsAndFreeShorthands        PASS  (--human, -d, inherited -o all parse)
=== RUN   TestParentPersistentOutput            PASS  (-o out.txt honored on child)
=== RUN   TestShortHParsesAsHelp                PASS  (-h prints help, never reaches RunE)
=== RUN   TestShorthandCollisionPanicsDocumentsTheHazard  PASS  (h / o cases still panic — documented hazard)
PASS  ok  fsdu  0.003s
```

Edge cases tested: root-level help; `-h` short form on a subcommand; long-only flag coexisting with auto-help; a genuinely free shorthand (`d`); persistent parent claim (`o`) inherited without redeclaration; and both forbidden redeclarations (`h`, child-side `o`) confirmed to still panic rather than silently misbehave. Caveat discovered while building the harness: `ExecuteC()` on a subcommand redirects to the root, so smoke tests must execute from the root with the full command path.
